mathematics.assertion_tested: On all 21 previously matched MIGHTEE/FASHI/ALFALFA galaxies, compare actual MIGHTEE and ALFALFA profiles with identical frequency-derived velocity windows and residual baseline treatment; test line-wing, baseline and aperture explanations of the flux difference.
mathematics.coefficient_domain: float64; frequency MHz; Jy spectral density; velocity relative to MIGHTEE frequency c*(nu_center/nu-1), hence same axis for both instruments; report Jy km/s in this relative convention plus Jy Hz.
mathematics.conventions: Integrate native channels by exact overlap of channel frequency-bin edges with common velocity window; no interpolation for flux integrals. Rebin onto common 20 km/s bins only for profile shape plots, preserving overlap integrals. ALFALFA flux is already baseline subtracted: compare residual rebaselining as primary and restoring supplied baseline then fitting same constant/linear rule as sensitivity. MIGHTEE beam arrays handled as CFG302; flag placeholder/invalid beam channels, do not conceal missing coverage.

analysis_specification.disclosure: Prior catalogue ratios and CFG302 diagnostics have been seen. This is an exploratory follow-up, not an independent prospective confirmation. No channel fluxes were compared before fixing these rules.
analysis_specification.population: All 21 triple matches, retain flagged objects; report 14 reliable, 10 reliable ALFALFA-code1, and original science subset separately. Do not require a new cube detection.

Rebin onto common 20 km/s bins only for profile shape plots, preserving overlap integrals. controls: Known flat/sloped baseline and line recovery
Native integral equals sum of common rebin integrals
ALFALFA spectrum integrated flux versus independent published catalogue
MIGHTEE old narrow-window extraction reproducibility for previously measured objects
Frequency grid and beam units/header verification
Mask ALFALFA -999 flux/baseline and low-weight channels
analysis_specification.interpretation: A cause is supported only if the paired flux ratios move toward unity consistently across reliable code1 galaxies and sensitivities. Wing and baseline contributions are signed differences in paired native-channel integrals. Larger apertures are noise-sensitive and can include neighbours. No assertion that flux is physically resolved out or continuum filtering is established by an image-cube deficit.
